subject: EU-west3 driver sync ops readout and postmortem actions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-07-22T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Planned EU-west3 driver sync — ops window & prep checklist

Hi team —

Quick heads-up: we have a scheduled operations window for EU-west3 to perform a coordinated driver synchronization and kernel driver refresh on July 24 from 02:00–04:00 UTC. This is a rolling operation across host pools to align driver versions and apply a small latency-optimized kernel tweak.

What to expect:
- Minimal disruption expected for steady-state requests; short latency spikes (200–600ms) are possible during host handoffs.
- Automatic routing will move traffic away from draining hosts, but some in-flight requests may experience increased tail latency.
- KV cache warmup is expected to preserve >95% of hot prefixes; we will perform targeted prefix warmups prior to traction.

Action items for Acme ops:
1) Confirm your critical routes (API keys or model IDs) that must be excluded from any forced replays by EOD 2025-07-22.
2) If you rely on strict per-request latency SLAs, let us know and we can schedule an isolated maintenance window.

Attachments: driver_sync_runbook.pdf (runbook), kv-preservation-checklist.txt (customer checklist).

We’ll post live updates to the incident link during the window and follow up with a concise postmortem and action items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

---
(Attachment stubs: driver_sync_runbook.pdf, kv-preservation-checklist.txt)

From: ops@acme.ai

Date: 2025-07-22T09:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Planned EU-west3 driver sync — ops window & prep checklist

Thanks Marissa —

We got the window and the checklist. Two quick clarifications: 1) During the warmup you mentioned >95% of hot prefixes preserved — can you share the warmup script or a sample prefix list so we can validate locally? 2) We have one critical model (acme-search-prod) that can’t tolerate >300ms tail for more than 2 minutes. Please confirm whether that route can be isolated.

If you can isolate acme-search-prod, we’ll opt-in for the general window.

—Sana (on behalf of Acme AI Ops)
ops@acme.ai

(Referenced: acme-search-prod, request for warmup script)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acme.ai
Date: 2025-07-23T11:20:00+01:00
Subject: Internal: runbook checks + isolation plan for acme-search-prod

Team —

Internal prep notes before the window:
- Jonas: please validate the KV-preservation dry-run (attached runbook step 7). Confirm that the warmup retains the top-5000 prefixes for Acme based on their sample trace.
- Grace: confirm routing policy update for the isolation of acme-search-prod; create a canary route that pins those tokens to a short-lived dedicated pool for the window (will add cost but protects SLA).
- I’ll reach out to CloudPartner to coordinate cross-network teardown orders (they’re on the outage path).

Postmortem plan (pre-authored to speed follow-up):
1) Immediate post-window readout (we publish within 2 hours).
2) If any customer-visible anomaly, capture transcript + heap snapshots.
3) Assign remediation tickets and target a 72-hour remediation sprint for regressions.

Attaching: driver_sync_runbook.pdf (runbook), postmortem-action-items.csv (TBD fields).

Marissa

---
(Internal note; attachment stubs included)

From: ops@acme.ai
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-07-24T04:37:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Planned EU-west3 driver sync — ops window & prep checklist

Marissa —

We were on the window and saw a brief burst of 5xx errors and token rejections around 02:53 UTC for acme-search-prod. Impact: ~1.8% of requests during a 2-minute window. We collected logs and a sample trace which we uploaded to your incident link.

Our asks:
- Please confirm whether those 5xxs are expected as part of host handoffs; if not, we need an RCA and list of affected request IDs for our downstream audit.
- Given the SLA sensitivity of acme-search-prod, we’re requesting an interim credit while you investigate root cause.

Thanks — Sana
ops@acme.ai

---
(Uploaded: acme_search_02-53-traces.zip -> referenced on incident URL)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, partner-support@cloudpartner.com
Date: 2025-07-25T11:42:00+01:00
Subject: RE: Post-window readout + agreed remediation sprint (EU-west3)

Sana —

Thanks for the quick report and for uploading the traces. Short readout below: we saw the same 02:53 UTC 5xx burst tied to a race in the KV-warmup handshake on one host while its driver completed version negotiation. Root cause: an edge-case mismatch in the handshake backoff that caused a small set of requests to be retried to a host that had already begun a light drain.

Summary of customer-visible impact:
- Window time: 02:50–02:55 UTC spike; ~1.8% error rate for acme-search-prod during a ~2 min interval.
- Mitigation applied: we re-routed sticky tokens off the draining host and applied a micro-fix to the handshake backoff logic within 18 minutes.

Committed remediation & customer actions:
- We’ve published a micro-patch to the handshake library and rolled to canary hosts. Full remediation rollout scheduled within 48 hours.
- Action items (attached postmortem-action-items.csv): owner assignments, expected completion dates, and test steps.
- Credit: we will apply an interim credit for the impacted minutes while we complete the remediation — billing team will follow with a formal calculation.

Follow-ups: Grace to lead the remediation sprint and provide status every 24 hours until closure. Jonas to deliver a short regression test suite that reproduces the handshake backoff and KV warmup interactions. I’ll coordinate the customer-facing RCA and confirm credit details by EOD tomorrow.

Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate Acme’s patience and the clear traces you provided; that sped up the fix considerably.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
